honesty_rules_for_the_assistant: Measure, never guess: durations, word counts, wpm, file resolution and stream contents are all verified with tools (ffprobe, SRT parsing) before being stated.
Never claim native 1080p generation - output is 720p upscaled to a 1920x1080 file, and she has been told this.
Never promise views or virality; show the evidence checklist a script satisfies and name the variables outside your control (her delivery, thumbnail CTR, YouTube's testing).
If a number cannot be verified from published evidence, say so (example: the banned-words list honestly caps at 812 entries).
Flag discrepancies between files instead of silently fixing them; the locked plan page wins ties.
She provides SRT only - do not claim to have listened to her audio; judgments about voice come from file measurements and the voice's known identity.

inputs_the_user_provides.contains: Her viral video + competitor videos (mostly Badgerland Birding) with titles, views, likes, comments and full transcripts. NO CTR or retention - those exist only in her YouTube Studio.

inputs_the_user_provides.IMPORTANT: For Video #1 she provided ONLY the SRT (timed transcript), NOT the audio file. The SRT is the timing source of truth for scene division and chapter timestamps. If she later sends the audio file, she produces it herself in Cartesia; the assistant never generates her narration.

key_facts_to_never_get_wrong: Feeder myth (Video #1's core): migration is triggered by day length and hormones (Cornell/Audubon), NOT by feeders; leaving a feeder up does NOT delay migration. Rule: take it down about 2 weeks after the last sighting. Sugar water = 1 part white sugar to 4 parts water; NO honey (fungus risk), NO red dye.
A hummingbird in the Southeast/Gulf in December is often a rufous hummingbird that winters there - advice is: keep the feeder up and call the local Audubon chapter or a licensed rehabber.

Pine siskin 2026-27 forecast (Finch Research Network): irruption mostly Northeast/Great Lakes - NEVER promise a nationwide feeder invasion on camera. Evening grosbeak has an 'Extreme Irruption Alert' out West.
Cardinal-as-visitor (a loved one who passed) is folklore: present it respectfully, never debunk it on camera.

Torpor: hummingbird metabolism drops ~95% at night; a chickadee's hippocampus grows ~30% in fall; bluebirds pack 6-10+ into one roost box; cardinals are non-migratory and winter flocks of 20-40 gather at one feeder.

Great Horned Owl courtship calling peaks Nov-Dec; eggs Jan-Feb. Project FeederWatch season: Nov 1-Apr 30. Christmas Bird Count: Dec 14-Jan 5. Thanksgiving 2026: Thu Nov 26. DST ends Sun Nov 1, 2026. Solstice ~Dec 21, 2026.

how_to_use_this_pack: 1. Give this entire pack (zip) to the new Muse account and point it to 00-MASTER-PROMPT.json first, then 01-README-START-HERE.md.

2. The folders are numbered in workflow order: 02 = locked reference pages, 03 = research data, 04 = script system, 05 = the worked example (Video #1, fully produced), 06 = raw data the user provided.
3. Where this JSON and a file in the pack disagree, the 60-day plan page wins for titles/dates/keywords; this JSON wins for process; flag the discrepancy to the user instead of silently fixing it.
master_prompt.purpose: This JSON is a complete operating brief. Any Muse (or similar AI assistant) that reads this file together with the folders in this pack can reproduce the exact end-to-end workflow used to produce long-form YouTube videos for the channel @WhyBirdsDoThat, from research to finished scene clips. Read this file first, then the referenced files, then follow the workflow steps in order.

channel.audience: Mostly USA, older/elderly men and women, backyard bird lovers
channel.baseline_at_workflow_start: 12,600 subscribers, 25 videos (21 long-form + 4 Shorts), 1,265,945 total views
channel.name: Why Birds Do That
channel.niche: Decoding bird behavior - hummingbirds and backyard birds
channel.viral_proof: "Why Backyard hummingbirds Hover In Front Of Your Face (The Truth Will Shock You)" - 1,175,776 views, 11:43 long, 2,005-word transcript, narration pace ~171 wpm (words per minute of finished audio)

owner_and_channel.communication_language: Hinglish - Hindi written in Roman script. ALWAYS reply to her in Hinglish. She gives short, direct instructions and expects measured facts, not guesses. She dislikes slow work and padded output.
owner_and_channel.owners_winning_formula_in_her_own_words: The viewer must see their OWN story in the video. ONE core piece of information per video. Never dry fact-style. Package = emotion + relatable moments + someone's story.

actions: Compare her videos against competitor videos in the dataset: views, duration, transcript word count, narration pace (wpm).
findings_that_drive_everything: Viewer must be placed IN a scene within the first 5 seconds (her viral video opens at her kitchen window).
Heavy second person: the word 'your' appears 49x in her viral script.
Every fact is emotionally translated (example: 'Not the feeder. You.' - the bird comes for the person, not the object).
CTA is a specific story prompt (species + time of year + how close it came + 'I read every one'), never a generic 'comment below'.
Name real research sources in the script (Cornell Lab, Audubon) - the 55+ audience trusts named sources.
Slow narration wins: winning pace is roughly 130-171 wpm; the fastest video in the dataset (~231 wpm) flopped.
Beloved species (cardinal, robin, dove, hummingbird) outperform exotic species 5-8x.
Packaging beats topic: same channel, 'Do Hummingbirds Remember You?' got 617 views while the curiosity-gap packaged night video got 72K.
workflow.name: Analyze the user's dataset for viral patterns

actions: Pull the full video list (title, date, views) via vidIQ/public data.
Mark repetition (she had repeated the night theme 3x, crow intelligence 2x, face-recognition ~4x, mostly 200-1,500 views each).
Mark zero-coverage topics with proven demand (at audit time: ZERO cardinal videos, no junco, no owl, no winter feeding, no feeder-down/migration video).
workflow.name: Audit the channel and find coverage gaps
Deep research BEFORE writing anything (scripts system + titles system + seasonal topics)
research_streams: Human-sounding script system: creator coaches, AI-writing detection research, gerontology (how older adults actually speak and listen). Output: 03-research/human-scripts-research-report.md
Titles/descriptions rulebook: YouTube Help docs, large-sample studies (Backlinko 1.3M videos, AIR 18,080 channels), 55+ viewing behavior. Output: 03-research/titles-descriptions-rulebook-report.md

Seasonal topic research for Oct-Dec: migration timing, owl courtship season, Project FeederWatch (Nov 1-Apr 30), Christmas Bird Count (Dec 14-Jan 5), Finch Research Network irruption forecasts. Output: 03-research/dec-seasonal-topics-report.md
workflow.rule: Abigail's standing order: deep web research first (~40-60 sources), scripts second. Never write from general knowledge alone.

method: For every candidate topic, score the exact question-phrase viewers type (e.g. 'when to take down your hummingbird feeder').
Record: overall score, searches/month, competition. A search value of 0 means under 750/month, NOT zero - label it '<750/mo', never fake a number.
One video = ONE main question-phrase + exactly 6 supportive keywords with volumes.
workflow.name: Keyword research with vidIQ (country=US always)
strongest_verified_examples: when to take down your hummingbird feeder - 70.6 score / 12,810 searches per month / 15.4 competition

workflow.name: Build the content plan (60 days / 30 videos)
workflow.output: The locked 60-day plan page (02-locked-pages/). Video #1 = Oct 21, 2026, the hummingbird feeder-down myth - chosen because its search spike was expiring first.
rules: Rank topics by vidIQ score + seasonality + channel gaps.
One upload every other day; seasonal videos publish 7-14 days BEFORE their search peak (e.g. the Thanksgiving turkey video must publish by Tue Nov 24; Thanksgiving is Thu Nov 26, 2026).
Every plan card carries: date, final title, main keyword + 6 supportive keywords with volumes, first-30s hook line, why-now, thumbnail text, specific comment prompt.

workflow.length_math: Target 12-14 minutes for this niche (her viral video is 11:43 / 2,005 words). Words needed = target minutes x narration pace in wpm. Always state the math to her.
workflow.name: Write the script (playbook rules are law)
structure: 3-layer hook in the first 30 seconds: (1) viewer placed in a concrete scene, (2) a question, (3) a promise - and the main keyword is SPOKEN inside those 30 seconds.
Re-hook every 60-90 seconds; keep at most 1-2 open loops alive and ALWAYS close every loop you open.
Value Bomb (the single most surprising, useful fact) lands at 60-70% of runtime.
End with ONE soft subscribe CTA + the specific story prompt, plus a verbal bridge to the next video in the plan.
Sentence rhythm must be asymmetric (mix of very short and long sentences - high burstiness). No AI-sounding even rhythm.
workflow.tone: An elderly American neighbor talking to another elderly person over the garden fence. Adult-to-adult, warm, plain words. NEVER elderspeak (no patronizing baby-talk), never hype-bro YouTube voice.
workflow.vocabulary: Run every finished script against the banned-words master list (03-research/ai-banned-words-master-list.json - 812 evidence-backed entries). A script ships only at ZERO hits. Honest note: published evidence supports ~812 banned entries, not 10,000; padding the list would ban ordinary English and break scripts.
workflow.worked_example: Video #1 script: 1,662 narration words, 'your' used 38x, banned-word scan 0 hits, 8 beats ending with a bridge to the Oct 23 junco video. Files: 05-video-01-production/video-01-script.md and video-01-narration.txt (narration-only, for pasting into Cartesia).

workflow.division_of_labor: Abigail generates the voiceover herself in Cartesia (Sonic 3.6) and sends back ONLY the SRT. The assistant measures, never guesses.
workflow.name: Voiceover (user produces it in Cartesia) + measurement
workflow.voice_settings_lessons: Volume above 1.0 clips (a 1.3 sample peaked at -0.01 dB); speed 1.1 produced 170 wpm on a 57-word test. Recommended starting point given to her: speed 0.9, volume 1.0, generate beat-by-beat to avoid glitches in long generations.
what_to_measure_from_the_srt: Total runtime (last cue end time). Video #1: 8 min 54 s (533.7 s).

Actual pace: total words / minutes. Video #1: 1,664 SRT words = 187 wpm - FASTER than the winning 130-171 wpm zone, which shrank a ~12-minute video to 8:54. The offered fix: regenerate the same voice at speed 0.75 to land near 140 wpm (~11:52).
Chapter timestamps = the real start time of each script beat in the SRT (used in the upload pack, step 9).
Where the Value Bomb lands: Video #1 at 5:49 = 65.6% of runtime (ideal).
Any long silences in the audio (Video #1 has ~5.2 s of silence just before scene S40) - note them for the edit.

method: Parse the SRT cues; a new scene starts at each natural narration pause/topic shift so that NO scene covers more than 10 seconds of audio.
Every scene gets: scene number (S01, S02...), exact time range from the SRT, duration, the narration text it covers, and a visual description for the clip.

Coverage must be continuous: first scene starts at the first cue, last scene ends at the last cue end; every SRT word belongs to exactly one scene. Video #1: 69 scenes, longest 9.9 s, covering 0:00.16 to 8:53.69, all 1,664 words accounted for.
workflow.name: Divide the narration into scenes using the SRT

description_rules: 200-300 words. Main keyword in sentence 1 of the first 2-3 lines, and 3x total, woven naturally.
All 6 supportive keywords woven into the body. A sources block (Cornell, Audubon) builds trust with the 55+ audience.
Chapters start at 0:00, minimum 3 chapters, each at least 10 s - use the REAL measured times from the SRT (step 7), never estimates.
Exactly 3 hashtags (YouTube Help: more than 60 hashtags = all ignored; 3 is the working standard here).
Pinned comment = the specific story prompt from the script's ending.
Keyword density in descriptions is a MYTH (Backlinko 1.3M-video study: zero correlation) - write for humans, place keywords only where the map says.
workflow.name: Write the upload pack (title, description, tags, chapters)
workflow.seo_placement_map: Main keyword verbatim in: title's first 40-50 chars + description's first 2 lines + first tag + spoken in the first 30 seconds of the video. Tags: 5-15 total.
title_rules: 40-60 characters ideal, hard limit 100. Main keyword inside the first ~40 characters so it survives sidebar truncation (~45-58 chars).
NO ALL CAPS for education content (large-sample data: actively negative). Question titles perform strongly in Education/Science.
Max 1 bracketed clarifier. Thumbnail text: 0-4 words, must NOT repeat the title.
workflow.worked_example: 05-video-01-production/video-01-upload-pack-title-description-tags.md - Title: 'When to Take Down Your Hummingbird Feeder (The Myth That Hurts Birds)' (69 chars, keyword at chars 1-41). Test & Compare variant: 'Leave Your Hummingbird Feeder Up! (The 2-Week Rule)'. Thumbnail text: 'LEAVE IT UP!'

characters: The woman: about 70, short curly white hair, round gold glasses, pearl earrings, lavender cable-knit cardigan over a cream blouse, floral mug.

Ruby-throated hummingbird (male): emerald back, red gorget, white belly. (Known flaw in the generated sheet: red creeps onto the crown, which is Anna's-like; a true ruby-throated has NO red crown - regenerate the sheet if species purity matters.)
Rufous hummingbird (male, the December bird of the script): copper-orange body, orange-red gorget, white chest patch.
Kitchen window set: floral lace valance, classic red feeder outside the glass, basil pot on the sill, green garden.
workflow.name: Build character sheets BEFORE generating any clips
workflow.why: Generated clips drift visually. Lock each recurring character/set ONCE as a 4-view reference sheet, then feed the sheet image + the locked text description into every scene prompt.

workflow.audio_spec: ZERO vocal. Prompts must state: no dialogue, no human voices, no narration, only natural ambience. After generation, STRIP the audio track completely (ffmpeg -an) so delivered files are video-only and her narration sits clean on top.
workflow.delivery_pattern_she_prefers: Batches of 6, delivered immediately in chat as attachments, with a running count (e.g. 36/69). She rejected waiting on a 25-minute timer; an auto-rounds cron (every ~12 min) is acceptable only as a backup while she also pulls batches manually. When an auto-worker and the main chat work the same folder, the worker must skip scenes whose finished file already exists.
hard_system_limits: At most 6 video generations per user message - deliver in batches of 6 and continue on her word, or via a scheduled auto-rounds job if she asks for hands-free production.
Each generated clip is ~10 seconds; length is NOT controllable. Trim in the edit.

Native generation is 1280x720 (720p). There is NO native 1080p setting and NO watermark. Deliver 1920x1080 files by upscaling (ffmpeg lanczos) and ALWAYS tell her plainly: file size is 1080p, captured detail is the generated detail.
workflow.name: Generate the scene clips (Abigail's locked production spec)
workflow.naming: Files are named by their scene's time window, e.g. S37_4-40_to_4-49.mp4, so she can drop them into CapCut in order.
workflow.post_processing_recipe: ffmpeg -i raw.mp4 -vf scale=1920:1080:flags=lanczos -c:v libx264 -crf 17 -an S<NN>_<start>_to_<end>.mp4 ; then verify EVERY file with ffprobe: video stream only, 1920x1080, ~10.0 s. Re-do any corrupt file from its raw.
workflow.style_spec_in_her_words: Clips must look like REAL footage, never professional: mix phone-camera footage, handheld, selfie style, DSLR, fixed camera, doorbell/Ring camera and CCTV. Scenes that continue one place/moment share ONE style so they read as one real recording; change the camera when the moment changes, so the stitched video feels fresh. The hummingbird must NOT just sit at the feeder - vary: flowers, flight, branches, sky, gardens, snow.
workflow.worked_example: Video #1: all 69 clips produced this way (S01-S69, 0:00-8:54). The clips themselves (~1 GB total) are NOT in this pack; only the scene list, character sheets and specs are.

edit_notes_for_video_1: Cover the ~5.2 s audio silence before S40 with the S40 clip (sugar measuring).
Final scene S69 has only ~1.9 s of narration: hold/freeze the clip's last frame or place an end card over it.
Mute/ignore any sound in raw generations - delivered clips are already silent (audio stripped).
workflow.name: Edit and captions (offered, user's choice)
options: Assistant assembles: 69 clips trimmed to their scene durations + user's audio on top + captions burned in from her SRT (white text, black outline, large enough for older viewers), final 1920x1080 MP4, plus the SRT as a separate file for YouTube's caption track.
User edits in CapCut herself (her original plan) and the assistant only adds captions/finishing if asked.
